points.why: Separates 'why fade' (structure, via a causal-loop sketch) from 'would another semester fix it' (change over time, via a stock-and-flow model of skill gained versus decayed).
Says a knowledge graph records facts and answers by lookup, and that it does not explain causes or project forward.

Covers scattered records and multi-hop queries, plus guardrails for deterministic, sourced answers. It omits frequently changing facts and joining outside data such as district records, and doesn't frame the graph as a data source alongside the models.
Recommends a mechanism-mapping session with tutors and teachers before any build, mentions a simple stock-and-flow model, and defers storage decisions with plain tables first.

pitfalls.why: Explicitly calls the graph the wrong tool for the causal question.
